intro.title: Type React props for reusable button
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a reusable Button component in React with TypeScript. You will learn how to define and use TypeScript interfaces to type the component's props, ensuring it accepts specific data like labels and click handlers. The core concept is using TypeScript's static typing to make your React components more predictable and easier to debug. You'll work with React functional components, TypeScript interfaces, and event handlers to create a button that can be customized across your application.
intro.usecase: Typing React props for reusable buttons is a fundamental pattern in building scalable design systems and component libraries, such as those used in enterprise dashboards, e-commerce platforms, and admin panels. For example, a dashboard might use a typed Button component with props for variants (primary, secondary), sizes, and disabled states across filter controls, data export actions, and modal triggers. This ensures consistency, prevents runtime errors, and simplifies maintenance when teams need to update button behavior or appearance globally. As a developer, you'll apply this daily to create reliable, self-documenting UI components that accelerate feature development and reduce bugs in production.
